messages:
Navya Patel: Hey team — first week snag. My kubectl context keeps flipping and AWS SSO creds expire after ~10m while I tail logs in namespace `redwood-app`. On mac M1 with zsh. Anyone seen this?

Priya Singh: Hey Navya :wave: Which context are you on? Can you paste `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config get-contexts` (or `kubectl config view --minify --flatten`) so we can check the exec plugin?

Navya Patel: Current context: `arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev`
`kubectl config get-contexts` shows:
```
CURRENT   NAME                                                           CLUSTER                 AUTHINFO
*         arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev       redwood-dev-cluster     arn:aws:eks:...-sso
          arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-prod      redwood-prod-cluster    arn:aws:eks:...-sso
```
When I run `kubectl logs -f` it works for a few minutes then `error: You must re-authenticate (error: exec plugin has expired credentials)`.

Samir Chen: Sounds like the exec credential helper issues short-lived creds. Try `aws sso login --profile redwood-dev` first. Also ensure your `aws` CLI is the recommended one (we've seen brew versions on M1 behave weirdly).

Miguel Torres: We have a small helper in the devex repo: `scripts/kube/login.sh` — it runs `aws sso login` and writes a stable per-user context like `navya-redwood-app` that pins the namespace. From repo root: `./scripts/kube/login.sh navya-p`.

Priya Singh: Short-term I can create a namespace-scoped RoleBinding giving you `view` in `redwood-app` so you can tail logs without cluster-wide perms. Want that or prefer to debug SSO?

Navya Patel: GitHub handle is `navya-p`. I ran `aws sso login` (opens browser) but still get re-auth error ~8m into streaming. Not sure why it drops mid-stream.

Priya Singh: Two quick things: 1) create a named context that sets `namespace: redwood-app` so accidental context switches won't change your namespace; 2) I'll grant `view` in `redwood-app`. Run locally to create a context alias (I'll handle the RoleBinding):
```
kubectl config set-context navya-redwood-app --cluster=redwood-dev --user=arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:node/placeholder --namespace=redwood-app
kubectl config use-context navya-redwood-app
```
The placeholder user will be replaced by the exec plugin once your SSO session is valid.

Priya Singh: Update: created RoleBinding `redwood-app-view` granting `view` to `navya-p` in `redwood-app`.

infra-bot: [system] rolebinding/redwood-app-view created by Priya Singh at 2026-03-23T12:34:50Z

Navya Patel: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-app` now shows pods. `kubectl logs -f` still dropped once but after re-running `./scripts/kube/login.sh navya-p` and `kubectl config use-context navya-redwood-app` it stayed stable. Much better, thanks!

Priya Singh: Great — if it flakes DM me and I'll grep the auth-proxy logs. I'll also add a note to `/docs/onboarding/kube-sso.md` about running the helper on M1.

Navya Patel: Will update my onboarding checklist. Thanks everyone :tada:
